questions.question_text:
Evaluate the following limits:
(i) lim_{x→3} [√(x² + 7) - 4] / (4x - 12)
(ii) lim_{x→-5} (3x³ - 4x² + 5x - 6) / (2x³ + 9x² - 4x + 1)
(iii) lim_{x→0} (6 sin 4x · tan 2x) / (5x²)
questions.official_solution_excerpt:
(i) Direct substitution gives 0/0. Rationalize numerator with [√(x² + 7) + 4]: numerator simplifies to x² - 9 = (x - 3)(x + 3) and denominator 4(x - 3)[√(x² + 7) + 4]. Canceling (x - 3) and substituting x = 3 yields 6 / [4(4 + 4)] = 6/32 = 3/16.
(ii) Direct substitution at x = -5: numerator = 3(-125) - 4(25) + 5(-5) - 6 = -506; denominator = 2(-125) + 9(25) - 4(-5) + 1 = -4, so ratio = -506 / -4 = 253/2 = 126.5.
(iii) Rewrite (6/5) · (sin 4x / x) · (tan 2x / x) = (6/5) × 4 × 2 = 48/5 = 9.6.
marking_scheme: Identifies 0/0 indeterminate form and rationalizes numerator
Factors (x - 3)(x + 3) and cancels (x - 3) cleanly to get 3/16
Evaluates rational limit by direct substitution at x = -5
Applies standard trigonometric limits sin(ax)/ax → 1 and tan(bx)/bx → 1 to get 48/5

questions.question_text:
Evaluate the following limits:
(iv) lim_{n→∞} [(2n + 1)(5n - 2)(n - 6)] / (n³ + 2n - 1)
(v) lim_{x→∞} (4x² + 2x - 1) / (3x² + x - 2)
(vi) lim_{x→2} (x² - 1)
questions.official_solution_excerpt:
(iv) Expanding leading terms gives 10n³ / n³. Dividing numerator and denominator by n³ as n → ∞ yields 10 / 1 = 10.
(v) Divide numerator and denominator by highest power x²: lim_{x→∞} (4 + 2/x - 1/x²) / (3 + 1/x - 2/x²) = 4/3.
(vi) Direct substitution at x = 2 gives 2² - 1 = 3.
marking_scheme: Identifies dominant degree n³ and divides by highest power to evaluate 10
Divides quadratic rational expression by x² to obtain 4/3 as x → ∞
Applies direct substitution for polynomial limit at x = 2 to obtain 3

questions.question_text:
a) Differentiate y = √(2x) from first principles.
b) Find dy/dx and d²y/dx² if x = t + sin t and y = t - cos t.
c) The radius of a sphere increases at 2.5 m/s. Find the rate at which (i) surface area and (ii) volume are increasing when radius r = 10 m.
questions.official_solution_excerpt:
a) y + Δy = √(2(x + Δx)). Rationalizing [√(2x + 2Δx) - √(2x)] / Δx gives 2 / [√(2x + 2Δx) + √(2x)]. As Δx → 0, dy/dx = 2 / (2√(2x)) = 1 / √(2x).
b) dx/dt = 1 + cos t, dy/dt = 1 + sin t, so dy/dx = (1 + sin t) / (1 + cos t). Differentiating wrt t and dividing by dx/dt gives d²y/dx² = [cos t(1 + cos t) + sin t(1 + sin t)] / (1 + cos t)³ = (1 + cos t + sin t) / (1 + cos t)³.
c) A = 4πr², dA/dt = 8πr(dr/dt) = 8π(10)(2.5) = 200π m²/s. V = (4/3)πr³, dV/dt = 4πr²(dr/dt) = 4π(100)(2.5) = 1000π m³/s.
marking_scheme: Sets up difference quotient [√(2x + 2Δx) - √(2x)] / Δx and rationalizes
Takes limit Δx → 0 to obtain dy/dx = 1 / √(2x)
Applies parametric chain rule dy/dx = (dy/dt) / (dx/dt) and computes d²y/dx²
Computes dA/dt = 200π m²/s and dV/dt = 1000π m³/s

(ii) Inverse trig rule: dy/dx = 1 / [|x|√(x² - 1)].
(iii) dy/dx = -2 sin x.
(iv) Power rule: dy/dx = 4x³ - 15x⁴ - 2.
marking_scheme: Applies chain rule to sin(cos x) to obtain -sin x cos(cos x)
States derivative of inverse secant sec⁻¹(x) as 1 / (|x|√(x² - 1))
Applies basic trigonometric and power rules accurately

questions.question_text: Find the minimum and maximum turning points of the curve y = x²(3x² - 3) = 3x⁴ - 3x², and check using the second derivative test.
questions.official_solution_excerpt: Expand y = 3x⁴ - 3x². First derivative dy/dx = 12x³ - 6x = 6x(2x² - 1) = 0 gives x = 0, x = 1/√2, x = -1/√2. Second derivative d²y/dx² = 36x² - 6. At x = 0, d²y/dx² = -6 < 0 (local maximum at (0, 0)). At x = ±1/√2, d²y/dx² = 12 > 0 (local minima at (±1/√2, -3/4)).

Classifies (0, 0) as local maximum and (±1/√2, -3/4) as local minima

Evaluate the definite integral using substitution:
∫₀¹ 2t² √(1 - 4t³) dt  (or general indefinite form ∫ 2t² √(1 - 4t³) dt).
questions.official_solution_excerpt:
Let u = 1 - 4t³, then du = -12t² dt ⇒ 2t² dt = -du/6.
Indefinite integral: ∫ (-1/6) u^(1/2) du = (-1/6) · (2/3) u^(3/2) + C = -(1/9)(1 - 4t³)^(3/2) + C.

questions.question_text:
a) Integrate ∫ (x + 2) / (x² - 5x + 6) dx using partial fractions.
b) By integration by parts, evaluate:
(i) ∫ x ln(x) dx
(ii) ∫ sin⁻¹(x) dx
questions.official_solution_excerpt:
a) Factor denominator: x² - 5x + 6 = (x - 2)(x - 3). Set (x + 2)/[(x - 2)(x - 3)] = A/(x - 2) + B/(x - 3) ⇒ x + 2 = A(x - 3) + B(x - 2). At x = 2, -A = 4 ⇒ A = -4. At x = 3, B = 5. Integral = -4 ln|x - 2| + 5 ln|x - 3| + C.
b)(i) Let u = ln x (du = 1/x dx) and dv = x dx (v = x²/2). ∫ x ln x dx = (x²/2) ln x - ∫ (x²/2)(1/x) dx = (x²/2) ln x - x²/4 + C.
(ii) Let u = sin⁻¹ x (du = 1/√(1 - x²) dx) and dv = dx (v = x). Integral = x sin⁻¹ x + √(1 - x²) + C.
marking_scheme: Factors x² - 5x + 6 = (x - 2)(x - 3) and finds constants A = -4, B = 5
Integrates partial fractions to -4 ln|x - 2| + 5 ln|x - 3| + C
Selects u = ln x and dv = x dx in integration by parts to obtain (x²/2) ln x - x²/4 + C
Integrates sin⁻¹ x via parts to obtain x sin⁻¹ x + √(1 - x²) + C

questions.question_text:
a) Explain what you understand by the limit of a function, and evaluate lim_{x→7} (x² - 49) / (x - 7).
b) Explain how to identify points of discontinuity of a rational function f(x) = p(x)/q(x) and state the intervals where it is continuous.
questions.official_solution_excerpt:
a) The limit lim_{x→a} f(x) = L describes the value f(x) approaches as x gets arbitrarily close to a from both left and right. Factoring x² - 49 = (x - 7)(x + 7), canceling (x - 7) for x ≠ 7 gives lim_{x→7} (x + 7) = 14.
b) A rational function p(x)/q(x) is discontinuous wherever the denominator q(x) = 0 (real roots r₁, r₂, ...), and continuous on all open subintervals (-∞, r₁), (r₁, r₂), (r₂, ∞).
marking_scheme: Defines limit conceptually as approaching value as x → a
Identifies denominator zeros q(x) = 0 as discontinuity points and lists continuous intervals

ii) [cos(t + h) - cos t] / h = [cos t(cos h - 1) - sin t sin h] / h → -sin t as h → 0.
iii) At t = 3: position x(3) = 27 - 12 + 6 = 21 ft. Velocity v(t) = dx/dt = 3t² - 4, so v(3) = 3(9) - 4 = 23 ft/s.
marking_scheme: Derives dy/dx = 8x + 2 using difference quotient for 4x² + 2x + 1
Applies cos(t + h) identity and standard trig limits to obtain -sin t
Evaluates position x(3) and velocity dx/dt at t = 3 seconds

questions.question_text:

questions.official_solution_excerpt:

b) List and explain four (4) types of system model.

questions.official_solution_excerpt: Data are raw unprocessed facts (e.g., individual test scores), whereas information is processed, meaningful data (e.g., class average report). questions.question_text:
a) Explain briefly the following processing techniques and list three advantages for each:
(i) Batch processing, (ii) Time-Sharing, (iii) Decentralized processing.
b) Distinguish between On-line processing and Real-time processing and give two application areas for each.
questions.official_solution_excerpt:
a) Batch processing groups transactions and runs them together (advantages: efficient off-peak CPU usage, low operator supervision, high throughput for payroll/billing). Time-sharing slices CPU time across multiple concurrent users (advantages: interactive responsiveness, fair resource sharing, reduced idle time). Decentralized processing places compute nodes at branch departments (advantages: local autonomy, lower WAN congestion, fault isolation).
b) On-line processing accepts inputs directly while connected to the host; Real-time processing guarantees immediate response within strict deadlines (e.g., airline seat reservation, ATM/air-traffic control).
marking_scheme: Defines batch, time-sharing, and decentralized processing with 3 advantages each
Contrasts on-line processing vs strict-deadline real-time processing with two valid application areas each

questions.question_text:
a) Explain the five (5) stages of Penetration Testing.
b) Explain four (4) types of firewall and list how SQL Injection can be prevented.
c) Mention five (5) ways of preventing a Ransomware attack.

a) Pen testing stages: Reconnaissance/Planning, Scanning, Gaining Access (Exploitation), Maintaining Access, and Analysis/Reporting.

questions.question_text:
a) Define: (i) Next-Generation Firewall (NGFW), (ii) Proxy Firewall, (iii) Network Address Translation (NAT) Firewall, and (iv) Stateful Multilayer Inspection Firewall.
b) Explain how SQL works on a website and list six (6) methods to prevent SQL Injection.
questions.official_solution_excerpt:
a) Proxy firewall acts as an intermediary inspecting Layer 7 traffic; NAT firewall hides internal private IPs behind public addresses; Stateful multilayer inspection tracks connection state across transport/application layers; NGFW integrates deep packet inspection, IPS, and application awareness.

Explains website SQL interaction and lists six valid SQL injection countermeasures

questions.question_text:
a) What is Hashing and discuss two primary uses of Hashing.
b) What is the MD5 Algorithm and explain the four steps that constitute its working.
questions.official_solution_excerpt: Hashing transforms variable-length input into a fixed-length digest using a one-way mathematical function. Primary uses: password storage verification and file/message integrity checks. MD5 produces a 128-bit digest through four steps: (1) Appending padding bits to 448 mod 512, (2) Appending 64-bit length, (3) Initializing 4-word buffer (A,B,C,D), (4) Processing 512-bit blocks in 4 rounds.
marking_scheme: Explains password verification and data integrity checking
Describes MD5 128-bit digest and padding/length/buffer/block-processing steps

questions.question_text:
Practical — Student Management Program:
Write a Java program that defines a Student class with Student name, Matriculation number, and three examination scores. Accept details, calculate total and average scores, display student details/average, and display a grade based on the average.

Practical — Inheritance and Method Overriding:
Create a superclass named Employee with calculateSalary(). Create subclasses FullTimeEmployee (fixed monthly salary) and PartTimeEmployee (hours worked × hourly rate). Override calculateSalary() in both subclasses and demonstrate polymorphism through an Employee reference.

Practical — Exception Handling:
Write a Java program that requests two numbers from the user, divides the first by the second, handles division by zero using exception handling with an appropriate error message, and uses a finally block to display a completion message.
Explain the four major principles of object-oriented programming. Give a practical example of each.
questions.official_solution_excerpt:
- Encapsulation: combining data and methods while restricting direct access to internal state (e.g., private balance with deposit/withdraw methods).
- Inheritance: allowing a subclass to acquire properties and methods from a superclass (e.g., Car extends Vehicle).
- Polymorphism: allowing a single reference type or interface to represent different object behaviours (e.g., Shape.draw()).
- Abstraction: exposing essential functionality while hiding complex implementation details (e.g., abstract class or interface).

questions.question_text: Differentiate between method overloading and method overriding. Provide Java code examples.
questions.official_solution_excerpt:
- Overloading: defining multiple methods with the same name and different parameter lists within a class (compile-time resolution).
- Overriding: redefining an inherited superclass method in a subclass with the same signature (runtime polymorphism).
Example: int add(int a, int b) vs double add(double a, double b) for overloading; @Override void speak() in Dog extends Animal for overriding.

questions.question_text: Explain inheritance in Java. Discuss its advantages and the different forms of inheritance that can be represented in Java.
questions.official_solution_excerpt: Inheritance allows a subclass to reuse fields and methods from a superclass using extends. Advantages: code reuse, maintainability, and hierarchical modelling. Forms in Java: single, multilevel, and hierarchical class inheritance (multiple inheritance is represented via implementing multiple interfaces rather than extending multiple classes).

questions.question_text: What is exception handling? Explain the functions of try, catch, finally, throw, and throws.
questions.official_solution_excerpt:
Exception handling manages runtime errors gracefully without crashing the program.
- try: encloses code that may throw an exception.
- catch: handles a matching exception type.
- finally: executes cleanup code regardless of whether an exception occurred.
- throw: explicitly throws an exception object.
- throws: declares checked exceptions a method may propagate to its caller.

questions.question_text: Differentiate between an abstract class and an interface in Java.
questions.official_solution_excerpt:
- Abstract class uses the abstract keyword; interface uses the interface keyword.
- Abstract classes can hold instance fields and constructors; interfaces define contracts (and can include abstract, default, static, and private methods).
- A class can extend only one abstract/concrete class, whereas it can implement multiple interfaces.

questions.question_text: Explain Java collections. Discuss ArrayList, LinkedList, HashSet, and HashMap.
questions.official_solution_excerpt:
The Java Collections Framework provides reusable data structures and algorithms:
- ArrayList: dynamic resizable array offering fast index-based access.
- LinkedList: doubly linked list efficient for frequent insertions/removals at ends or iterators.
- HashSet: hash-backed Set storing unique elements with no guaranteed order.
- HashMap: key-value map storing unique keys mapped to values for fast lookup.

questions.question_text: Explain constructors in Java. Differentiate between default constructors, no-argument constructors, and parameterised constructors.
questions.official_solution_excerpt:
A constructor is a special block with the same name as its class (and no return type) invoked automatically to initialise new objects.
- Default constructor: compiler-generated no-arg constructor inserted only when no constructors are defined.
- No-argument constructor: explicitly written constructor taking zero parameters.
- Parameterised constructor: accepts arguments to initialise object fields with custom values.

questions.question_text: Differentiate between a program and a process. Explain the common states of a process.
questions.official_solution_excerpt: A program is a passive set of stored instructions on disk, whereas a process is an active executing instance with allocated CPU state, registers, and address space. Common process states: New (being created), Ready (awaiting CPU), Running (executing instructions), Waiting/Blocked (awaiting I/O or event), and Terminated (finished execution).

questions.question_text: Explain the functions of a compiler, assembler, linker and loader.
questions.official_solution_excerpt:
- Compiler: translates high-level source code into assembly, intermediate, or machine code.
- Assembler: converts assembly mnemonics into machine-code object files.
- Linker: resolves external references and merges object files and libraries into an executable.
- Loader: places the executable into main memory, sets up execution context, and begins execution.

questions.topic_name: OS Services, System Calls & I/O Handling
questions.question_text: Discuss process scheduling and explain First Come First Served, Shortest Job First and Round Robin scheduling.
questions.official_solution_excerpt:
Process scheduling decides which ready process receives CPU time to maximise utilisation, throughput, and responsiveness.
- FCFS: non-preemptive queue serving processes in arrival order.
- SJF: prioritises the process with the shortest estimated CPU burst.
- Round Robin: assigns each ready process a fixed time quantum in cyclic rotation.

questions.topic_name: OS Services, System Calls & I/O Handling
questions.question_text: Explain memory management and discuss paging, segmentation and virtual memory.
questions.official_solution_excerpt:
Memory management tracks, allocates, protects, and reclaims main memory across processes.
- Paging: divides logical memory into fixed-size pages and RAM into frames to eliminate external fragmentation.
- Segmentation: divides memory into logical variable-sized regions (code, stack, data).
- Virtual memory: abstracts RAM using disk backing so processes enjoy larger isolated address spaces.

questions.topic_name: OS Services, System Calls & I/O Handling
questions.question_text: Define deadlock. Explain its four necessary conditions and describe ways of preventing or avoiding it.
questions.official_solution_excerpt: Deadlock is a state where processes wait indefinitely for resources held by one another. Four necessary conditions: (1) Mutual exclusion, (2) Hold and wait, (3) No preemption, (4) Circular wait. Prevention breaks at least one necessary condition (e.g., strict resource ordering); avoidance checks allocation safety (e.g., Banker's algorithm) before granting resources.
marking_scheme: Mutual exclusion and Hold and wait
